A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Meta-Expert research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results on three LTSSL datasets, pseudo-label diagnostics, module ablations, and FreeMatch-based evaluations in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark accuracies in Tables 4–5, ablations in Tables 6–7, and Appendix C evaluations in Tables 8–9.

M1.justification: The three experts, DEA assignment module, weighted-logit aggregator, MFF module, losses, warm-up, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 receives grammatical edits only.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10-LT, STL-10-LT, and SVHN-LT under the same distribution scenarios. Adding '-LT' to dataset names in table captions clarifies existing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain supervised and FixMatch/FreeMatch references alongside SAW, Adsh, DePL, ACR, BaCon, CPE, and SimPro. Expert and oracle comparison rows are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported splits, sample counts, imbalance ratios, metrics, architecture, and training settings remain unchanged in Sections 4.1–4.2. Appendix C retains the same FreeMatch evaluation settings.

E4.justification: The expert-selection diagnostics, feature-depth analysis, DEA/MFF ablations, feature-combination comparison, and computational-overhead analysis are retained without additional or revised analyses.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 in both versions specifies three different random seeds and reporting means and standard deviations. No uncertainty-reporting practice or statistical procedure changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9, plotted findings, and computational-overhead results retain the same values. For example, first-column Meta-Expert accuracies remain 74.39±0.46 in Table 4 and 75.68±0.28 in Table 8.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 and Appendix D retain the same definitions, assumptions, theorem, lemmas, and derivations. Equation 18 is split across pages in v3, without mathematical changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same DEA/MFF contributions, novelty assertions, generalization-bound claim, and benchmark-performance claims.

C2.justification: Explanations of expert specialization, depth-dependent bias, MFF's behavior under inverse distributions, and computational tradeoffs remain unchanged. No substantive limitations or qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility details are retained. The same code URL moves from the abstract to a footnote in Section 3.3; the USB reference remains, so access information is neither added nor removed.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix B, and the references retain the same cited works and positioning, including distinctions from CPE, RIDE, SADE, and BalPoE.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited grammatical and terminology corrections, including 'affects' to 'affect' and 'hyper-parameters' to 'hyper-parameter'. The code statement moves to Section 3.3; the narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is enlarged, Algorithm 1 moves between columns on page 6, and Tables 3–5 and 8–9 receive caption edits. Spacing and page breaks change, including splitting Equation 18 across pages 15–16; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves readability through a larger Figure 2, consistent LT dataset captions, and relocating the awkwardly split abstract code sentence to Section 3.3. Scientific evidence and reproducibility information are preserved. Splitting Equation 18 across two pages is a small presentation drawback, but the overall gains remain limited and positive.
